feature_notes:
Adds usable per-save ZIP compression control to ordinary, write-only and loaded edited Python workbooks: book.save(path, compression_level=3). None retains default level 6; integers 1 through 9 use Deflate; 0 uses ZIP Stored. Invalid types/ranges reject before replacing a target or consuming write-only resources. Ordinary and loaded books support repeat saves with different levels. Untouched original package entries retain their compressed bytes.

Published wheels use pure-Rust zlib-rs explicitly. Source builds may select native zlib with --no-default-features --features deflate-zlib and a C toolchain. The former zip deflate feature already used zlib-rs, so this is not a claimed backend-only speedup; unused Zopfli support is removed. Backend choice is compile-time.

Pins canonical Rust alpha.4 commit 0a4eadc87387af286065e0a8380a9c2b6cccfc30. Native million-numeric-cell creation: zlib-rs level 6 is 0.9200 s / 2,942,935 ZIP bytes, level 3 is 0.2487 s / 3,299,121 bytes. Native A1 edit/save: 1.3052 s versus 0.7529 s with nearly unchanged ZIP size. These exclude Python conversion and are not end-to-end Python timing claims. Native zlib is not universally faster; higher levels do not guarantee smaller files. All uncompressed part hashes and CRCs agree across numeric, mixed and editing workloads. See canonical benchmarks/alpha4-compression.md.

Selected compatibility checks pass against installed candidate wheels on CPython 3.11 through 3.15 (currently RC), with focused compression tests covering public readback, ZIP method, invalid-option target protection and retry. Both core backends pass Rust 1.88 on Linux and Windows. Ruff format/check, Rustfmt and strict Clippy pass.

Release tests all 25 wheels across Linux x86_64/ARM64, Windows x86_64 and macOS Intel/Apple Silicon using five shared-compilation jobs, plus an independent sdist, before PyPI OIDC publication. Rust core MSRV remains 1.88; Python wheels use latest stable Rust.

Memory limits, formula-cache invalidation, original assets, worksheet spools and atomic output staging remain intact. Full structural/style/feature compatibility remains staged. Test consolidation and M2 closure are deferred to alpha.5; M2 remains open.
